notes: §1985:XII.3.3 SR1 (kb/Work PB5422, landed): a REPLACE 'must be preceded by a separator period except when it is the first statement in a separately compiled program'. ApplyReplaceStatements asks the constructs row replace-anywhere-2002 of a REPLACE that FollowsSeparatorPeriod rejects, and FollowsSeparatorPeriod now asks the COPY-expanded resultant text whatever file each character came from: a REPLACE that begins library text follows what preceded the COPY statement (DISPLAY "X" COPY LIBR. is refused, COBOL0900; DISPLAY "X". COPY LIBR. is accepted), and a debugging line's carrier is stepped over like a separator, so a REPLACE on a debugging line after a period is accepted. Witnesses: 1985-SR-XII_3_3-1, pb5085-replace-not-after-period, pb5422-replace-library-text-not-after-period, pb5422-replace-library-text-after-period.

next.reason: 1985: "It must be preceded by a separator period except when it is the first statement in a separately compiled program."; 2023: "A REPLACE statement shall be preceded by a space except when it is the first statement in a compilation group.". 2023 drops the required preceding separator period and needs only a space. It also allows REPLACE where a separator may appear and in library text, so more programs are accepted.
